doc.title: Bob Hardaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: Film and theater work now support the Los Angeles musicians' union
summary: Motion pictures and good theater are keeping local musicians busy and paid well in Los Angeles.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Yeah, right now because of the motion pictures and because of theater, theater is very good in Los Angeles now, and that’s about the only thing that is very good now in Los Angeles, so the motion picture industry, the musicians that are being employed are really supporting our local union here, and that’s good, because the guys that are on the inside of that field are keeping very busy now, they’re doing well. So that’s all good stuff. And then as I say the theaters, the major theaters like the Schubert and so forth, they have very good scales too. Some guys can make a really nice living by doing one of these shows that runs a year or two you know. So that’s the best part of the business right now I think.
